name: Amstrad CPC
description: Amstrad's 8-bit home computer range, launched in the UK in 1984 with the CPC 464. It was sold as a complete package with its own monitor and built-in tape or disk drive, which made it popular in the UK, France, Spain and Germany. Later models added 128 KB and 3-inch floppy drives.

specs.media: Cassette (built in on the 464), 3" floppy disk

curiosities: The computer drew its power from the supplied monitor, so the two were sold as a set.
It used Hitachi-format 3-inch floppy disks rather than the more common 3.5-inch format.
In Germany it was sold under the Schneider brand.
The 1990 GX4000 console and CPC Plus range were built on upgraded CPC hardware.
